architecture_decision: hot path is CPU-bound (AVX2 only); GPU/CAGRA reserved exclusively for background batch refit (Section 4.4) and Control Plane (Dataiku) historical batch search

combined_hot_path_layer1_plus_layer2.note: sum of independently measured means; not yet measured as a single fused pipeline call, which would be the next verification step

architecture_history: original hypothesis (unverified): CAGRA wins as historical index scales to 10k-100k+ points
measured finding: CAGRA never wins at query batch_size=1, regardless of index size up to 500,000 points; brute_force always wins at batch=1
measured finding: CAGRA wins decisively at query batch_size>=1000 (background/batch workloads)

architectural redesign: hot path no longer searches the full historical index at all; background GPU refit (HDBSCAN via cuML, at batch sizes where CAGRA is measured to win) periodically compresses the historical attractor map into ~50-100 centroids with per-centroid anomaly radii (epsilon)
hot path now performs O(K) centroid lookup (K~100) via AVX2 instead of O(N) or O(log N) search against the full historical index
measured result: centroid lookup at K=100 costs 0.233us mean, beating the lead's <0.5us target by more than 2x
combined Layer 1 + Layer 2 hot-path latency: approximately 2.1us, matching the lead's production-readiness estimate
not_yet_done: the two layers have only been measured independently; a single fused end-to-end timing (Layer 0 ingest -> Layer 1 -> Layer 2 lookup -> Layer 4 decision, all in one measured call) has not been performed
no CPU pinning or real-time kernel tuning applied to any measurement in this report
the background GPU refit path that produces the centroid+epsilon map has not yet been implemented in C++; only the CPU-side consumption of that map (centroid lookup) has been built and measured

argmin over K=100 centroids is done with a scalar loop, not vectorized reduction; this was a deliberate simplicity choice given the negligible cost at this K, not yet benchmarked against an AVX2 horizontal-reduction alternative
